records.name: The Falkirk Wheel
records.description: The Falkirk Wheel is a rotating boat lift in Tamfourhill, Falkirk, in central Scotland, connecting the Forth and Clyde Canal with the Union Canal. It opened in 2002 as part of the Millennium Link project, reconnecting the two canals for the first time since the 1930s.
records.hours: Visitor centre open daily 10am-5:30pm; boat trips run Apr-Oct

records.name: The Kelpies
records.description: The Kelpies are a pair of monumental steel horse-heads between the Scottish towns of Falkirk and Grangemouth. They stand next to the M9 motorway and form the eastern gateway of the Forth and Clyde Canal, which meets the River Carron here. Each head is 30 metres (98 ft) high and weighs approximately 300 tonnes (47,000 st).

records.name: Helix Park
records.description: The Helix was a land transformation project to improve the connections between and around 16 communities in Falkirk Council, Scotland, including the eastern end of the Forth and Clyde Canal, and to regenerate the area near where the canal joins the River Carron. The most visible feature of the development is the two unique equine sculptures known as The Kelpies.

records.name: Callendar House
records.description: Callendar House is a mansion set within the grounds of Callendar Park in Falkirk, central Scotland. During the 19th century, it was redesigned and extended in the style of a French Renaissance château fused with elements of Scottish baronial architecture. However, the core of the building is a 14th-century tower house.

records.name: Callendar Park
records.description: Historic parkland around Callendar House with woodland walks, play areas, formal grounds and stretches of the Antonine Wall earthworks.

records.name: Falkirk Steeple
records.description: The Falkirk Steeple is a municipal building on the High Street in Falkirk in Scotland. The building, which accommodates a heritage centre, is a Category A listed building.

records.name: Rough Castle Roman Fort
records.description: Rough Castle Fort is a Roman fort on the Antonine Wall roughly 2 kilometres south east of Bonnybridge near Tamfourhill in the Falkirk council area, Scotland. It is owned by the National Trust for Scotland.

records.name: Antonine Wall
records.description: UNESCO World Heritage Roman frontier running across central Scotland; the Falkirk district contains some of its best-preserved ramparts, ditches and fort sites.

records.name: Seabegs Wood
records.description: Woodland section of the Antonine Wall corridor with peaceful walking paths and visible traces of the Roman frontier near Bonnybridge.

records.name: Camelon Roman Fort
records.description: Site of an important Roman fort and settlement at Camelon, associated with the Antonine Wall frontier and later military activity.

records.name: Falkirk Stadium
records.description: The Falkirk Stadium is an all-seater football stadium in Falkirk, central Scotland, which is the home ground of Scottish Premiership club Falkirk and Lowland Football League club East Stirlingshire since 2018. The stadium has a capacity of 7,937 and currently consists of three fully completed stands.

records.name: Union Canal
records.description: The eastern canal linked to the Falkirk Wheel, popular for towpath walks, boat trips and views over the surrounding countryside.

records.name: Forth and Clyde Canal
records.description: Historic sea-to-sea canal crossing Falkirk, central to the area's industrial heritage and now a scenic route for boating and walking.

records.name: Torwood Castle
records.description: Torwood Castle is a ruined 16th-century L-plan castle near the village of Torwood, in the Falkirk Council area of central Scotland. It was designated as a Category A listed building in 1979. The Buildings at Risk Register for Scotland originally listed its level of risk as low, but raised that level to moderate in mid-2019 after seeing signs of continued neglect.

records.name: Dunmore Pineapple
records.description: Eccentric 18th-century garden folly topped with a giant stone pineapple, one of Scotland's most distinctive architectural curiosities.

records.name: Falkirk Museum and Gallery
records.description: Local museum displays and gallery spaces interpreting Falkirk's Roman, industrial and social history.
records.address: Callendar House, Callendar Park, Falkirk FK1 1YR

records.name: Dollar Park
records.description: Traditional town park with bandstand, play areas, bowling greens and a Victorian layout close to central Falkirk.

records.name: Watling Lodge
records.description: Important Antonine Wall site where ditch, mound and fortlet earthworks are especially easy to read in the landscape.

records.name: Bonnyside Roman Wall
records.description: Quiet Roman frontier section near Bonnybridge with surviving embankments and a strong sense of the wall's line.

records.name: Laurieston Village
records.description: Planned industrial village east of Falkirk with broad streets and heritage tied to the Carron ironworks and docks.

records.name: Larbert Old Church
records.description: Historic parish church site reflecting Larbert's older village identity before railway-era expansion.

records.name: Larbert House
records.description: Former country house estate remembered through surviving grounds and its role in Larbert's local history.

records.name: Carron Works Heritage
records.description: Industrial heritage stop recalling the famed Carron Company ironworks, cannon foundry and carronade production.

records.name: Bo'ness and Kinneil Railway
records.description: Volunteer-run heritage railway with steam and diesel trains through historic dockland and estate scenery.

records.name: Kinneil House
records.description: Historic house with links to the Hamilton family and James Watt, standing within the wider Kinneil estate.

records.name: Kinneil Museum
records.description: Small museum introducing the archaeology, industry and social history of the Kinneil estate and Bo'ness foreshore.

records.name: Rosebank Distillery
records.description: Revived Lowland whisky distillery on the canal, celebrated for its historic name and waterside setting.

records.name: Airth Castle
records.description: Historic tower-house and later mansion in the countryside north of Falkirk, known for its long noble associations.

records.name: Muiravonside Country Park
records.description: Wooded country park with river gorge walks, ornamental gardens and family-friendly outdoor space on Falkirk's eastern side.

records.name: Polmont Woods
records.description: Local woodland walking area offering peaceful trails and glimpses of the wider Avon and Union Canal landscapes.

records.name: Callendar Walled Garden
records.description: Restored walled garden area beside Callendar House, adding formal planting to the broader parkland visit.

records.name: Falkirk Trinity Church
records.description: Prominent town-centre church and civic landmark on the High Street, continuing Falkirk's long parish tradition.

records.name: Westquarter Glen
records.description: Wooded glen on Falkirk's western side with streams, bridges and quieter local walking routes.

records.name: Dunipace Old Parish Church
records.description: Historic church site near Denny and Bonnybridge, tied to the district's older rural communities.

records.name: Grangemouth Heritage Walk
records.description: Self-guided heritage area through the old canal and dock town, useful for understanding Grangemouth's industrial rise.

records.name: Helix Lagoon
records.description: Waterside section of the Helix landscape with paths, bridges and reflective views toward the Kelpies.

records.name: Falkirk Tunnel
records.description: Historic tunnel on the Union Canal route, linking Falkirk with one of Scotland's most impressive surviving canal engineering works.

records.name: Antonine Wall at Callendar Park
records.description: Stretch of the UNESCO-listed Roman frontier preserved within Callendar Park's grounds.

records.name: Antonine Wall at Rough Castle
records.description: Perhaps the most dramatic Antonine Wall landscape in the district, combining fort, ditch and outworks in one visit.

records.name: Seabegs Roman Fortlet
records.description: Smaller Roman fortlet site at Seabegs, adding archaeological depth to walks along the Antonine Wall corridor.
